newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond volatilities slip in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond volatilities slip in slow trade.

text.p: Uninspiring comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan hit implied volatilities on U.S. Treasury bond options, particularly in the short end, traders said Thursday.

Anticipation of Friday's 1996 fourth quarter advance gross domestic product report failed to pump up volatilities, but traders said vols may firm going into next week's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, the Fed unit that sets interest rate policy.
"Volatilities are definitely down," one trader said. "The market goes up and volatility goes down."
Greenspan told the Senate finance committee the Fed still considers the consumer price index to overstate inflation by 0.5 to 1.5 percentage points a year.
"Greenspan didn't say anything," a trader said. "Some people are looking for a strong GDP report tomorrow but I don't know what that does to the market."
He said some dealers believe a strong number would send the market down on the belief that strong economic growth could tip the Fed's hand toward a rate increase.
"But then again maybe it doesn't go down because it takes away from first quarter growth," he said. "So nobody wants to do a whole heck of a lot of anything."
The average forecast for the advance GDP is for growth of 3.9 percent.
One bond options trader said Greenspan's comments convinced more market participants that an interest rate increase was not around the corner.
Implied volatility in March T-bond futures options traded up to 11 percent intraday before easing back to about 10.80 percent, up fractionally from Wednesday's 10.75 percent.
Traders said few big blocks crossed but several investors were buying up the March 112 calls.
"Today was overall a pretty blase day," one trader said.
Implied volatilities for Eurodollar futures options slipped across the board, continuing the trend seen Wednesday.
Implied volatilities for June Eurodollar futures options fell to around 11.40 percent from 11.70 percent Wednesday. They reached 11 percent intraday.
For September Eurodollar futures options, implied volatilities slipped to the 14.3 percent area from about 14.6 percent Wednesday.
